newsitem.title: UK: IBCA rates Krung Thai Bank C individual.
newsitem.headline: IBCA rates Krung Thai Bank C individual.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Tuesday it assigned an individual rating of C and a legal rating of 2 to Krung Thai Bank, Thailand's second largest bank.

"The individual rating is an evaluation of a bank's financial strength based on the premise that the bank is entirely independent and therefore unable to rely on the support of state authorities or its owners," IBCA said in a statement.
An Individual rating of C is given to a bank "which has an adequate risks profile but possesses one or more troublesome aspects, giving rise to the possibility of risk developing," IBCA said.
Krung Thai is Thailand's second largest bank and is 61 percent owned by arms of the Thai government. It has about 14 percent market share in both loan and deposit markets.
"The bank's performance has improved dramatically since the early 1990s, with management having restructured its balance sheet by placing a greater emphasis on lending," IBCA said.

Funding is sound, underpinned by Krung Thai's access to government deposits and government employees' payroll. In addition, Krung Thai is in the process of shedding much of its public sector culture, IBCA said.
However, IBCA said it is concerned about the bank's continuing large overhang of non performing loans and the thinness of its reserves, given the impending economic slowdown.

The expected loss on non performing loans has declined as a percentage of the total loan book from 3.6 percent to 2.4 percent; nevertheless this implies a total level of non performing loans of perhaps eight percent, IBCA said.
Moreover, when one allows for the more lenient definition of non performing loans in Thailand, loans in arrears by 90 days or more may easily exceed 10 percent of loans.
In Thailand, loans are only considered to be non performing after twelve months, or six months in the case of unsecured loans.

Regarding its reserve levels, IBCA said "Krung Thai does not maintain a provision much greater than the minimum Bank of Thailand requirement and therefore its profitability could be more markedly affected than some of its better reserved peers, should the impending economic slowdown prove severe, it said.
"The individual rating takes account of the possible adverse affects on Krung Thai from the impending economic slowdown in Thailand," IBCA said.
